Using the herdr App: A Step-by-Step Interactive Guide

app.Rmd

Introduction

The herdr Shiny application provides an interactive spreadsheet and visualization environment for modeling livestock greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, upstream feed LCA & water deprivation (EF 3.1 / AWARE), energy requirements, agroecological land competition, and edible protein outputs.

Instead of manually editing multiple CSV files in a text editor, this guide walks you through setting up, validating, and evaluating your livestock system using the graphical interface.

1. Initializing Your Workspace

Before building your farm scenario, launch the application and configure your baseline parameters:

  • Launch the application: Open the tool from your R console by running herdr::run_herdr_app(), or access the cloud-hosted version at juancbm99.shinyapps.io/herdr.
  • Establish your baseline (Step 1: Data Source): Choose to load a predefined package example (Blank_IPCC_2019, Level1_Spain_Dairy_Cattle_2015, Level2_Spain_Dairy_Cattle_2015, Monogastric_Example, Video_Example), upload your existing CSV project files, or clear all data to start from scratch.
    • Tip: Loading Blank_IPCC_2019 provides all 42 standard ruminant and monogastric animal_tag cohorts pre-populated with their valid animal_type, animal_subtype, production_role, and default replacement_rate values (population = 0), so you only need to enter headcounts for the cohorts present on your farm!
  • Configure farm parameters (Step 2: Configuration): Specify the farm’s country (farm_country), the FAO reference year (year), and the IPCC Global Warming Potential standard (AR6, AR5, AR4, or SAR). Check Use automatic herd cycle if you only declare adult breeding animals in Census and want herdr to calculate replacement and offspring populations automatically (see Herd Demography & Population Dynamics).

2. Building Your Farm Scenario

Navigate left-to-right through the top tabs. Every cohort is uniquely identified across tables by the four keys farm_id, animal_tag, region, and subregion.

  • Declare your herd (Census): Create a row for each distinct animal cohort.
    • Enter farm_id (e.g., farm_1), animal_tag (e.g., mature_dairy_cattle), and optionally region and subregion.
    • Enter the Average Annual Population (AAP) in population.
    • Row Order Matters: The top-to-bottom row order you set in Census is preserved in both output tables and all bar charts.
  • Structure the diets (Diet Profiles): Link your cohorts to a ration via diet_tag and define dry matter macro-shares (forage_share, concentrate_share, milk_share, milk_replacer_share). Ensure these four shares sum to 100%.
  • Specify feed items (Ingredients): Map specific feedstuffs to each diet_tag.
    • Select ingredient_type first (forage, concentrate, milk, milk_replacer); the ingredient dropdown automatically filters to matching feeds from Feed Char..
    • Ensure ingredient_share values sum to 100% within each ingredient_type.
    • Leave country_of_origin and custom_yield_kg_ha blank to let herdr trace origin dynamically via FAO trade data, or override either column with known farm data.
  • Input productive traits (Ruminants, Monogastrics & Weights):
    • Strict Taxonomy Dropdowns: To prevent classification errors, animal_type, animal_subtype, and production_role use strict dropdowns:
      • Ruminants (cattle, sheep, goat): animal_subtype must be dairy or meat.
      • Monogastrics (swine, poultry): animal_subtype automatically restricts to meat when animal_type is swine, and meat or layer when animal_type is poultry.
      • production_role: Strictly mature (breeding/milking/laying adults), replacement (growing future breeders), or slaughter (growing animals for meat).
    • Weights: Provide adult_weight_kg, initial_weight_kg, final_weight_kg, and productive_period_days (inter-parturition interval for breeding females except laying hens; commercial flock laying cycle for laying hens; days on feed for growing/slaughter stock).
  • Manage waste (Manure): Use the cascading dropdowns (system_base →\rightarrowsystem_variant →\rightarrowmanagement_months →\rightarrowsystem_climate →\rightarrowsystem_subclimate →\rightarrowclimate_zone →\rightarrowclimate_moisture) to select valid IPCC configurations, and ensure allocation sums to 1.0 per cohort.

3. Interactive Spreadsheet & Pre-Flight Health Checks

  • Direct Grid Editing & Guided Modal: Edit cells directly like Excel, or click Add Record to use a guided form with tooltips.
  • Column Header Tooltips: Hover over the info icon (i) next to any column header to view its definition and physical units, or consult the Data Dictionary tab.
  • Real-Time Pre-Flight Validation: Before running calculations, herdr continuously checks cohort keys, strict taxonomy values (animal_type, animal_subtype, production_role), IPCC coefficient compatibility, diet 100% sums, and manure 1.0 allocations. If any issue is detected, a badge appears on the tab and a Review button in the sidebar lets you jump straight to the table that needs attention.

4. Executing and Analyzing Calculations

  • Run the model (Step 3: Calculate): Select Full Assessment (generate_impact_assessment) or any individual physiological module and click Run Selected.
  • Explore the Results Tab:
    • Group Chart By: Aggregate bars dynamically by farm_id, animal_tag, animal_type, animal_subtype, region, or subregion.
    • Impact Category Selector: Switch between Carbon Footprint (GHG) (Scope 1 + Feed Fossil + Feed LUC), Land Use Footprint (Cropland vs. Convertible/Unconvertible Grassland), Water Deprivation (AWARE), Multi-Impact Overview (3-panel comparison), and Protein Feed Efficiency (Mottet FCR).
    • Functional Unit Selector: Benchmark impacts as Total Inventory (Gg CO2e, ha, Mm3 depriv.), Per Commercial Product (milk, meat, egg, wool), Per kg Edible Protein, or Per Animal Head.
    • Dual Output Tables (Table 1: Totals vs. Table 2: Product Intensities): Toggle between the Absolute Bio-Environmental Inventory (totals) and the Enterprise-Integrated Product Intensities (intensities) table below the chart (the table switches automatically when you select product, protein, or FCR views).

5. Exporting and Saving Your Progress

⚠️ Important Session Note: On the hosted web instance, all modifications reside temporarily in browser memory. Always download your files before closing or refreshing your browser tab.

  • Download Chart & Active Table: Export high-resolution PNG charts (300 DPI) and download either Table 1 (herdr_results_*.csv) or Table 2 (herdr_product_intensities_*.csv).
  • Back up your session (Step 4: Downloads): Click Download Input Data (ZIP) to bundle all your edited CSV tables into a ZIP archive that you can re-upload in future sessions.
